**Finding: Compliant — no redline proposed.**

The agreement contains no most-favoured-nation obligation burdening Meridian Fieldworks:

- **§ 12.3** affirmatively works in our favour: "Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment."
- **§ 7.1** (Fees fixed during the initial term; no undisclosed charges) and **§ 8.3** (renewal uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%) constrain Vendor pricing rather than requiring us to extend or match any third-party terms.
- Full-text searches for "most favoured", "favourable/favorable", "MFN", "no less", and "other customers" surfaced no hidden MFN mechanic anywhere in the document.

This matches the playbook's preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer), so no edit is required.

One note outside this rule's scope: §§ 2.2 (sole and exclusive provider) and 12.4 (24-month non-compete on Customer) sit in direct tension with the § 12.3 acknowledgement. They are not MFN provisions, but they should be picked up by the exclusivity and restrictive-covenant rules — and the § 12.3 disclaimer is a useful lever when negotiating their deletion.
